speaker: AURELIO
text: A man on a jury panel in Queens owes one of ours four hundred, and the case is nothing to do with us. We used to keep three or four like him and never spend one. He has asked whether the debt is still a debt.

speaker: AURELIO
text: Now, listen to me. A man under indictment keeps his habits — same bar, same hours, same Mass. It is the ones who change their pattern that a jury looks at twice. Your father never moved a chair.

speaker: AURELIO
text: There are sixty made men in this family and I can name every one. In your father's time I could name their wives as well. Two of ours married this year and nobody thought to tell me either time.

speaker: AURELIO
text: The Commission has let it be known the books may open this year, which has not happened since 1957. We have four men who have waited and three chairs, and all four have been told they are first.

speaker: AURELIO
text: The man who owns the linen building wants to sell and has offered it to us first, fairly. Your father rented every room he ever used. A deed sits in an office where anybody may walk in and read a name off it.

speaker: AURELIO
text: Letters keep coming to the club from a man in Dannemora, addressed to you by name, asking for commissary. He has nine years left. We answered every one of those once, and the answering was the point of it.

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: The kid who inherited our building has put the rent from ninety dollars to two hundred and told me he has an offer from a laundromat. Forty-one years we have sat in that room. He was born in Astoria.

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: Georgie Nardone was in the Camelot Saturday telling a story from 1959 with names in it, one of them mine. He has buried two brothers for this family. He isn't a bad man, kid. He's a drunk.

right.label: LET HIM TALK. HE'S EARNED IT

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: Two of the young guys bought the same car in the same colour and they park them outside the club side by side, like a showroom. I told them what that looks like and they laughed. In front of the room.

left.label: I'LL SAY IT MYSELF, IN THE ROOM

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: Every Christmas your father put an envelope in fifty-one hands and I wrote the list. I have written it again. Eleven of those names you have never met, and four of them are upstate.

right.label: THE LIST IS THE MEN WHO EARN

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: The other people want a man to sit on a thing in Bath Beach and they asked for me by name, not for you. It's an honour, kid. It's also the second time this year they have done that.

right.label: THEY ASK ME OR THEY ASK NOBODY

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: Carmela asked me at breakfast when I am going to stop. I told her when the kid tells me to. She would like you to know she asked, which is why I am telling you that she asked.

speaker: GIULIA
text: The nuns have put Anna forward for a scholarship to a school in Manhattan. The form wants your occupation and last year's income, in writing, signed by you, and it goes to an office downtown.

speaker: GIULIA
text: My father is selling the pharmacy, and the man buying it asked him whether the family would be a problem. He asked my father that, in his own shop. My father came to me instead of to you.

right.label: HE'S BUYING ON OUR AVENUE. HE PAYS

speaker: GIULIA
text: Paolo cut a photograph out of the paper — a man being walked out of a building on Withers Street — and wrote the man's name under it in his own hand. It was in his school book. I put it back.

left.label: SIT HIM DOWN AND TELL HIM WHAT WE ARE

right.label: THE BOOK GOES IN THE STOVE, NOTHING SAID

speaker: GIULIA
text: The man who drives me stands outside the shop door with his hands folded while I buy fish, and the whole avenue watches him do it. Take him off me, or tell me he is there for a reason.

speaker: GIULIA
text: Scavo's daughter has asked me to stand godmother to her baby. If I say yes I am at that family's table for the rest of my life, and so is Anna. If I say no, his wife knows why by Tuesday.

speaker: GIULIA
text: A woman telephoned this house at eleven at night and asked for you by your first name, and when I said who I was she apologised and rang off. I am not asking who she is. I am asking what I should have said.

speaker: MATTY
text: There's an old guy at the club who tells everybody he was in the war with your father. Your father wasn't in the war. He's eighty and everybody lets him, and now he's asking me for money on the strength of it.

speaker: MATTY
text: The girl I'm seeing has a brother who's a cop in Queens and he wants a beer with me. Not officially. He wants a look at the guy going with his sister. I said I'd have to see about Thursday.

speaker: MATTY
text: Somebody put the window through at the shoe place on Starr Street and the guy came to me instead of to you. I paid for the glass out of my own pocket and told him it was from you. Sixty-two dollars.

left.label: TAKE THE MONEY BACK. IT WAS FROM ME

right.label: NEVER PUT MY NAME ON YOUR MONEY

speaker: MATTY
text: I've been carrying a package for a guy in Ridgewood twice a week and he gives me twenty dollars for it. Tuesday I worked out that twenty dollars is nothing for what it probably is.

speaker: MATTY
text: Mucci sits at the club and watches the room and never says anything, and now the guys sit with their backs to the wall when he's in. I like him. I don't know whether I'm supposed to.

left.label: SIT WITH HIM. LET PEOPLE SEE

right.label: WATCH HIM AND TELL ME WHAT HE DOES

speaker: MATTY
text: My mother went and saw a man about a job for me at the Bulova plant. Forty-eight dollars a week and a locker with my name on it. She told him yes before she told me.

speaker: MATTY
text: I fixed the television at the club. Nobody asked me to. Now everybody watches the television and the card game broke up at nine two nights running, and the house takes a piece of the card game.

speaker: DUKE
text: There's a shop steward at the Bulova plant nine thousand into other men's insurance money, and he came to me. I've not put a dollar in front of him yet. He'd sign anything you like, boss. Anything at all.

speaker: DUKE
text: Forty locations in Ridgewood with twelve-year-old machines that eat the money, and the man servicing them is seventy-one and does it by kicking them. I've priced new ones and ordered nothing. People use the diner now.

speaker: DUKE
text: One of mine has been buying weight off a man in Bed-Stuy and selling it four blocks from your mother's church. I found out from a barber, boss, which is how everybody else finds things out.

right.label: HE KEEPS IT, AND HE'S QUIET

speaker: ADLER
text: The new manager at the bank on Myrtle asks where the cash comes from. Not on a form — out loud, at the counter, with a queue behind me. He is thirty-one and he believes he is being friendly.

speaker: ADLER
text: Your father bought four hundred shares of a shipping company in 1955 in his own name, and they are worth four thousand dollars today. Selling them takes a signature and a probate file a clerk reads.

speaker: ADLER
text: I have been offered a partnership in a practice in Kew Gardens — three men, real clients, a brass plate with my name on it. I would still keep your books. Not telling you would also have been a decision.

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: There's a fellow in my house sitting the lieutenant's exam in March who will pass it whether I like him or not, and then he has my night shift. He's from Staten Island and he doesn't drink.

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: My daughter's wedding is in June and the hall alone is twenty-two hundred dollars. I'm not asking you for anything. I'm telling you what June looks like from where I sit, and you can do as you please with it.

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: A raid card got written up for that place of yours on Woodbine and it has found its way into a tray where it will sit about a month. I'm telling you so that the month is a month and not a year.

left.label: MOVE THE GAME, AND THANK HIM

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: One of my patrolmen put a car through a shopfront on Wilson Avenue with a drink in him, and the shop is one of yours. If your man remembers it differently, the boy keeps his job and owes me one.

speaker: DET. RANIERI
text: I arrested a boy of seventeen on Menahan Street last night with a pistol in his belt he didn't know how to hold. He gave me your name. Not as an alibi — as a reference, the way you'd give a priest.

speaker: DET. RANIERI
text: There's been a car outside your linen plant three nights running with two men in it who are not from my squad and not from any squad in Brooklyn. I'd rather it was me who found out what they are.

speaker: CONCETTA
text: There is a woman at the ten o'clock who has taken to sitting in my pew, on my side, telling people she is a cousin of ours. She is not. She is frightened of somebody and she has decided the pew is a roof.

right.label: SHE CAN SIT THERE. NOTHING ELSE

speaker: ANGELO
text: A man I knew inside has offered me steady work and no questions about the eight years. I have not answered him and I will not answer him until you tell me what the answer is.

left.label: YOU'RE ON MY PAYROLL FROM FRIDAY

right.label: TAKE IT. I CAN'T CARRY YOU

speaker: ANGELO
text: Somebody in this family told somebody else I must have made a deal inside, and it came back to me the way these things do. I'd like to sit in a room with him and you, and have him say it to my face.

speaker: ANGELO
text: A man I did six years next to is running a book in Queens that pays nobody, and he has asked me to come in with him. I told him I'd ask you, which I think was the wrong answer, so here I am asking.

speaker: FALLON
text: The city is putting a container crane on Pier 4 that does the work of forty men, and my board want it struck before it's bolted down. A strike costs you six weeks of everything that moves through there.

speaker: FALLON
text: There's a coffee counter by the gate taking ninety cents a day off every man on the shape-up, and the fellow who owns it is nobody's friend. My men keep asking why we don't own it. I'd like to say we do.

speaker: FALLON
text: There's an officer on the Genoa run who'll carry whatever you like in his own cabin for two hundred a trip. He's done it a year for somebody else and would rather do it for us. He never asks what it is.

right.label: WE DON'T CARRY WHAT WE CAN'T SEE

speaker: DON BRACA
text: There is a man coming over next month who has to sit somewhere for a year, and everybody at that table has a reason it cannot be them. Your father took two of these for me and never once asked me why.

speaker: DON BRACA
text: My wife's nephew has a linen business in Astoria and yours is on Flushing Avenue, and the two of you are quoting the same three hotels. I would rather this was settled by young men than by old ones.

speaker: DON BRACA
text: There is a proposal at the table for two per cent of everything into a fund — lawyers, bail, the families of men inside. I intend to vote for it, and I would rather not be the only one who does.

speaker: MOE WILLS
text: Two of your young men came into a bar on Marcy asking for the man who writes the numbers there. He is one of mine, and he told them so, and they laughed at him. I'd rather correct mine than watch you correct yours.

speaker: ROSA
text: Two men ate in my dining room Saturday and told the boy to put it on your account. There is no account. I have written down what they ate on a piece of paper and I don't know whether to give it to you or burn it.

speaker: ROSA
text: My cook's boy comes in after school and sits where I can see him, because his mother works nights. He is eleven, he is very good with people's coats, and he has started listening to the back table.

speaker: FATHER COLLA
text: The school has forty children whose fathers are away, and we have started calling it that. Away. I wrote the word on a form myself last week without noticing. I thought you should know it has become a word.

left.label: THE PARISH GETS WHAT IT NEEDS

speaker: FATHER COLLA
text: There is a man who wants to be married in my church on Saturday to a woman the diocese does not consider free to marry, and he has told me you would want it done. I would like to know whether that's true.

left.label: I'D TAKE IT AS A FAVOUR

speaker: DR. NARDI
text: A man came to my surgery at nine with his hand wrapped in a towel and his wife waiting in the car. He asked for me by name and offered me sixty dollars. I have never seen him before. Somebody gave him my name.

speaker: DR. NARDI
text: Your uncle's blood pressure is what it is and he will not take the tablets, and he tells me his brother never took a tablet in his life. His brother is dead. I would like that said to him by somebody who is not me.

speaker: THE PHONE
text: It rings at the club and a man's voice asks for you by your full name, the way a hospital does, and when you take it there is nobody there. Three times this week, always at the same hour.

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: You've put your hand behind me in front of people this year, and here's what it bought you. Ferrara's crew came to me with a question last week instead of to you, and I answered it the way you would have.

speaker: AURELIO
text: Your uncle settled the thing between Ridgewood and the freight men on Tuesday, in your name, and exactly as you would have. I watched a man do that for another man in 1949. It is not the settling that matters.

right.label: NOTHING IS SETTLED IN MY NAME

speaker: DUKE
text: You told me once, formally, with a man stood there to hear it, and I've done what you said since. Now the fellow who used to buy off mine buys off Bed-Stuy, and my people watch the money go past the window.

speaker: DUKE
text: I told you about those lunches before anybody else could, and nobody has mentioned it since. The man has stopped calling — his boss died or he got bored. I'd like something for it, boss, in front of people.

left.label: GIVE HIM SOMETHING, WHERE THEY SEE

speaker: MATTY
text: I've got a button and a corner and I still get sent for the dry cleaning by guys who were made sixteen years ago. I'm not complaining. I'm asking whether I'm supposed to say no, because I don't know.

right.label: GO FOR THE DRY CLEANING ANOTHER YEAR

speaker: GIULIA
text: You told me a thing once that turned out not to be true, and I have never brought it up, and I am not bringing it up now. I am telling you that I have started checking. That is all I came in to say.

speaker: GIULIA
text: There are two Sunday tables in this family now and I am expected at both of them, and whichever one I sit at, forty people will read it as your answer rather than as mine.

speaker: ADLER
text: Both rooms send to me for figures now, and I have started keeping the Canarsie numbers on a page of their own so that the two answers match the two questions. That is a page a government lawyer enjoys.

left.label: ONE SET OF BOOKS. ONE ROOM

speaker: A SOLDIER
text: Nobody has told me where to stand. I've nine years in, a wife, and a corner, and both rooms have asked me to Sunday dinner this week. I came to you because you're the boss. That's still the case, right?

speaker: CONCETTA
text: My grandson comes out to me on the bus twice a week from his aunt's house in Ozone Park, on his own, because he asked to. He is thirteen. He sits with me and tells me about the school out there.

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: The number went up once and you paid it without making a face, which I noticed. Now there's a man downtown asking why the gambling arrests at the Eight-Three look the way they look, and asking it in writing.

left.label: GIVE HIM FOUR SMALL ONES OF OURS

speaker: DET. RANIERI
text: You know I've had your family in a drawer a while now. There's a boy of yours driving for a man he shouldn't drive for, and if I have to take somebody this year it'll be him. That isn't a threat, it's a diary.

left.label: THE BOY COMES OFF THE STREET

speaker: ANGELO
text: You put me back on and I've earned every week since, and nobody has said the word deal to my face in four months. Somebody said it behind my back to a man who told me. I know the name. I won't say it unless you ask.

speaker: FALLON
text: The fund has been borrowed against once, and the international sends auditors every second year, and this is the second year. I can lose the paperwork or I can find it for them. Losing it is the expensive one.

speaker: DON BRACA
text: I have put your name into rooms you were not standing in, which you know. There is a thing on Staten Island I would like done by somebody who is not mine, and I would like it done before Friday.

speaker: MOE WILLS
text: You said no to that business in front of your own people and I heard about it the same week. The man selling it on my streets asks nobody, and my people buy their numbers off him now because he's stood right there.

left.label: THAT HALF OF THE STREET IS YOURS

speaker: ROSA
text: You put a line through what I owed and I have never said thank you out loud, because I didn't know where to put it. There's a man eating in my dining room telling people he is the reason you did.

speaker: FATHER COLLA
text: I have buried two young men in five weeks, and both times the church was full of men who arrived in cars and left in cars. The second mother asked me not to let you in. I told her the church is not mine to close.

left.label: STAY AWAY FROM THE NEXT ONE

right.label: I'LL BE AT THE NEXT ONE

speaker: AURELIO
text: I have taken to writing the date at the top of every page, because I no longer trust myself to remember which day I wrote a thing. I would still rather you brought things to me. I would like you to bring them twice.

right.label: I'LL BRING YOU THE SMALL ONES

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: The doctor on Wyckoff has shut the office and gone, and there's a man in a room over the club tonight with a hole in him and nobody to telephone. Your father kept two doctors, kid. Two, because one of anything is none.

left.label: FIND ANOTHER DOCTOR. PAY WHAT IT TAKES

speaker: AURELIO
text: I have found the same question written in my own book twice, three weeks apart, in my own hand, with two different answers. I would rather you heard that from me than watched me do it in a room.

right.label: WE'LL GO THROUGH THE BOOK TOGETHER

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: Sacco gave a ruling at the table Thursday and sent us to a man who has been dead six years. Nobody said anything. Two capos looked at each other, and then they looked at me, kid. Not at you.

left.label: A YOUNGER MAN SITS BESIDE HIM

speaker: AURELIO
text: Now, listen to me. Men have begun asking me the same question twice, to see whether they get the same answer. I would rather be finished by you, at this table, than by a room that has stopped listening.

right.label: THEN IT'S FINISHED. AND THANK YOU

speaker: AURELIO
text: They have me at Wyckoff Heights and the priest has been twice, which tells you what the doctor won't. Ask me something. Anything at all. Let me be of use in a room one more time.

speaker: A SOLDIER
text: Two of ours went up to collect on the Bed-Stuy line Friday and came back without the bags. Nobody was hit and nobody was armed. They were told the arrangement is over, and told to say so.

left.label: THEY GO BACK TOMORROW, WITH PEOPLE

right.label: NOBODY GOES BACK UNTIL I'VE SPOKEN TO HIM

speaker: MOE WILLS
text: I didn't give that order, and I'm not going to punish the man who did, because he's twenty-six and he said out loud what the rest of them think. Your father and I had an understanding. He's dead, and so is it.

left.label: THEN WE'LL MAKE A NEW ONE

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: There's a man of ours in Kings County with his jaw wired and a man of theirs who won't walk again, and every crew is waiting on a word from this room. I've done this three times, kid. It's cheaper on Tuesday than Friday.

right.label: WE SETTLE IT AT A TABLE

speaker: DUKE
text: There's a bakery on Central Avenue that's been on my list since before either of us. Old man in the back, son on the counter. This week I found out whose father he is. That detective. Ranieri. Nobody told me.

right.label: HE PAYS LIKE EVERY OTHER SHOP

speaker: DET. RANIERI
text: My brother runs my father's bakery on Central Avenue and my father sits in the back of it, eighty-one years old. Somebody came in Tuesday and asked him about the arrangement. I'm asking you once, in the street.

right.label: EVERY SHOP ON THAT STREET PAYS

speaker: THE STREET
text: The bakery on Central Avenue had its window out on Sunday night and nobody who works for you can say who did it. The old man swept the glass up himself before the shops opened, and he has telephoned nobody.

left.label: STAND IN THE SHOP WHILE IT'S GLAZED

right.label: IT'S GLASS. IT ISN'T OUR BUSINESS

speaker: ADLER
text: The local you hold has nine hundred members, a welfare fund with two hundred thousand dollars in it, and an election in the spring that the Department of Labor sends an observer to. He stays four days.

left.label: THE ELECTION IS CLEAN AND WATCHED

speaker: THE PAPERS
text: LOCAL VOTE 891-14: 'THE MEMBERS HAVE SPOKEN,' SAYS NEW PRESIDENT. Page nine, four paragraphs, and a photograph of a hall with thirty men in it. Somebody at the Eastern District has cut it out and kept it.

left.label: NOTHING MOVES THROUGH THAT HALL FOR SIX MONTHS

right.label: WE CARRY ON. IT'S FOUR PARAGRAPHS

speaker: UNCLE SALLY
text: It's your uncle. It's eighty-one degrees, and there's a man down here from Cleveland who knows everybody we know, and he has asked me a question I would like to answer. Also nobody here can make a coffee.

right.label: YOU'RE RETIRED. SAY NOTHING TO ANYBODY

speaker: AURELIO
text: Your uncle has telephoned four men in this family this month from Florida. Three told me and one did not. Men were run from further away than that in your father's time, and nobody thought it strange either.

left.label: LET HIM TALK. HE'S EARNED IT

speaker: AURELIO
text: The boy's lawyer telephoned me before he telephoned the boy, which tells you the kind of lawyer he is. They have offered eighteen months instead of nine years, with a condition on it. There were no conditions once.

left.label: THE HOUSE PAYS TO FIGHT IT

right.label: LET HIM HEAR IT AND DECIDE LIKE A MAN

speaker: MATTY
text: It's me. They put a man in the room who wasn't a lawyer and he said a name and asked if I'd like to be home in the spring. I said I'd think about it, because I wanted to hear what else he'd say. I'm telling you first.

left.label: YOU COME HOME WHEN YOU COME HOME

right.label: IN THERE YOU'RE NOT MY SISTER'S SON

speaker: GIULIA
text: Your mother said her sentence on Sunday and it was not yours, and by Tuesday two women had asked me, kindly, whether the family is all right. I answered them both. I would like to know what I answered.

left.label: NOTHING IS WRONG IN THIS FAMILY

speaker: CONCETTA
text: I said what I said because your father would have said it, and because you never asked me not to. You may come on Thursday and eat, or you may leave me to be an old woman who was right. Both of those cost you.

speaker: DUKE
text: I counted Bushwick's envelope with two men watching and wrote the figure on the flap, the way we do. The figure that reached the book on Flushing Avenue was four hundred under mine. Three months running now.

left.label: COUNT IT IN FRONT OF THE BOOKKEEPER

right.label: WRITE YOUR FIGURE AND SAY NOTHING

speaker: ADLER
text: Four hundred dollars a month for three months. My daughter is at Barnard, the fees are twelve hundred a term, and I have never once asked this family for anything. I entered it as a loan to myself. In my own hand.

left.label: IT'S A LOAN. IT GETS PAID BACK

speaker: CONCETTA
text: Aurelio Sacco is in the ground and there is nobody left who tells you no, Nicola. Your father had two men who did it, and he shouted at both of them, and he kept both of them. Who says it to you now?

speaker: THE STREET
text: Nobody writes numbers on Marcy Avenue this week. Two candy stores have their shutters down at noon, the man on the corner by the church has gone to his sister in Newark, and the police park on the line now.

left.label: PULL OUR PEOPLE BACK OFF THAT LINE

speaker: DET. RANIERI
text: I'm not going to ask after your mother today. There's a file open with your name on the tab and I'll work it in my own time, and when it's ready I'll come to your door myself, and I'll be very polite about it.

left.label: GO TO HIS DOOR FIRST, WITH NOTHING IN YOUR HANDS

speaker: GIULIA
text: Paolo has asked to come back to Brooklyn and live with you. He is thirteen, he asked me in the kitchen in front of his sister, and he had plainly practised it. I said I would ask you, and I have asked you.

speaker: CAPT. KIERNAN
text: There's a statement in a folder downtown from a doctor on Wyckoff Avenue. Four pages, and it names shoulders rather than men, which is worse. I've read it. I can't take it out and I can't unread it.

right.label: LET IT SIT IN THE FOLDER
